Subject: SIG request: hosting boundaries & evidence for deployment modes

Hi Marissa,

We're working through the SIG for Glacier Therapeutics and have a few open questions around how Redwood maps to the SIG items for hosting/deployment boundaries (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC/on-prem). The SIG team wants: a short explanation of each mode, where customer data is stored/processed, network egress points, encryption-in-transit and at-rest specifics, and any customer-facing controls (KMS, HSM, VPC peering options).

Attached is our blank SIG template (we'll send the Excel separately). Can you point us to an internal doc or provide a concise write-up we can include in our evidence package? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min sync later this week.

Thanks,
Sam
Security Ops | Glacier Therapeutics

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a brief mapping and attached three artifacts (PDF exhibit, concise runbook, and a topology diagram) that you can reference directly in the SIG responses. High-level summaries below; the exhibit includes exact SIG question IDs and the corresponding evidence file names.

Summary (short form for SIG):
- Hosted (Redwood API - multi-tenant hosted): production inference runs in our hosted control plane. Customer data is processed on shared compute with tenant isolation at the application and network layer; we do not provision dedicated GPUs for hosted. Data at rest: short-lived KV caches and logs are ephemeral and encrypted with our service KMS; persistent customer data (if any) is not stored unless explicitly opted in (e.g., for fine-tuning). TLS 1.2+ enforced, internal mTLS between services. Evidence: redwood_sig_deployments_exhibit_2025.pdf (sections 2.1–2.4).

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): customers get reserved GPU pools and a logically isolated tenant slice. Compute nodes are single-tenant for that customer, though underlying hardware may be co-located in the same cluster. Data storage and KV caches are configured per-customer and encrypted; customers can request dedicated encryption keys (bring-your-own-key via KMS integration) for additional separation. Network egress: controlled via NAT gateways in the region; VPC peering and private links supported for Dedicated in supported clouds. Evidence: runbook-hosting-modes.md (dedicated section) + network-diagram-hosted-dedicated-private.png.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed network. Our software runs inside the customer's VPC or on-prem environment; no customer data leaves the VPC unless explicitly configured. Customers manage their own ingress/egress and may integrate with their KMS/HSM. We provide a private control plane option for audit/event collection only (optional and configurable). Evidence: runbook-hosting-modes.md (private section), installation checklist, and sample KMS integration logs (available on request).

Security controls and notes:
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ for client-server; service-to-service mTLS internally. Data at rest: AES-256 encryption, customer KMS supported for Dedicated and Private.
- Auth & keys: API keys for Hosted; mutual TLS and customer-managed auth solutions supported for Private.
- Audit / logs: request-level tracing and token-level cost/latency telemetry; audit logs can be exported to customer s3/Cloud Storage for Dedicated/Private.
- Custody boundary: exhibit includes a one-page custody diagram per mode.

Next steps:
1) I attached the three artifacts for direct upload into your SIG evidence column.
2) Karthik / Priyom are cc'd to confirm the Dedicated network bullet and the on-prem KMS flow; they can provide a short network flow statement for the SIG.
3) If you'd like a 30-min walkthrough, propose times and we'll set it up.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance (Programs) | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the write-up. A couple of short clarifications to surface in the SIG exhibit so Glacier has precise language:

- Dedicated: clarify that "single-tenant compute" means the GPU instance is provisioned for that customer but may share the same physical rack with other customers; we enforce strict cgroup/container isolation and kernel hardening. Add the exhibit note: "No cross-tenant kernel/module sharing; hypervisor-level isolation applied where VMs are used."

- Private (on-prem): highlight that we ship an air-gapped installer option for highly regulated customers; by default the private deployment uses a customer-provided VPC with optional egress controls turned on. For KMS: we support both API-based KMS calls and HSM-backed key wrapping; include sample log lines in the exhibit (redacted).

- Network egress: for Hosted we publish the set of egress IP ranges in our publications page and we can produce a signed statement of the ranges/ASN for the SIG.

I'll add two short paragraphs and updated diagram captions into the PDF exhibit and send the minor update by EOD.

-Karthik
